card: **свой** means *one's own* and points back to the subject of its clause: **Он чита́ет свою́ кни́гу** (his own). **Он чита́ет его́ кни́гу** means another man's book. In the third person the choice changes the meaning; with **я, ты, мы, вы** both **свой** and **мой, твой**… are fine.

sections.body: English *his* is ambiguous: *John took his coat* (his own, or someone else's?). Russian decides: **свой** if it belongs to the subject, **его́** if it belongs to someone else.

sections.title: The rules
sections.body:
- **свой** refers to the subject of the same clause: **Ма́ша позвони́ла свое́й ма́ме.**
- It's never part of the subject: **Его́ брат живёт в Москве́**, not ~~Свой брат~~.
- A new clause has a new subject: **Он сказа́л, что его́ сестра́ прие́дет.** (**сестра́** is the subject there, so **его́**.)

sections.title: Set phrases
sections.body: **свой** also means *one of us*: **Он свой челове́к.** And *each their own*: **У ка́ждого своё мне́ние.**

mistakes.why: With **его́**, Ivan loves another man's wife!
**свой** can't be part of the subject.

examples.en: We came in our own car.
